ground_truth.description: The refactor of test_release_probe_slot_called_on_runtime_error replaces the explicit `gate.detect_cap_hit = MagicMock(return_value=False)` with `_make_gate(...)`, but the new `_make_gate` factory does not set `detect_cap_hit`. As a bare MagicMock auto-attribute, `gate.detect_cap_hit(...)` now returns a truthy MagicMock instead of False, so any production branch that checks `detect_cap_hit` takes the opposite path (cap-hit detected), likely driving the escalation_created event and changing what the test actually exercises.

The `_make_gate` factory intentionally omits `detect_cap_hit` from its default attribute set, so it does not fully cover every UsageGate attribute a construction site may need; call sites that relied on `detect_cap_hit` returning a concrete False (rather than a truthy auto-mock) silently lose that behavior after routing through the factory.

TestMakeGateFactory pins account_count/active_account_name/soonest_resets_at/override passthrough but does not assert that the mock-driven branches (e.g. detect_cap_hit / cap-hit path) behave as the callers expect, so the contract test would not catch the missing detect_cap_hit default that changed runtime-error test behavior.

The task asked for one shared gate factory so attribute defaults like soonest_resets_at=None are set in one place. The change instead adds two byte-identical `_make_gate` copies (test_invoke.py:85 and test_steward.py:195), alongside the already-existing canonical `shared.testing.make_gate_mock` (which sets the same defaults plus detect_cap_hit, uses spec=UsageGate, and is already used by shared/tests) and shared/tests `_mock_gate`. A new UsageGate attribute still needs edits in multiple places, and the copies' docstrings falsely claim it 'only needs to be updated here'. orchestrator/tests/_orch_helpers.py already exists as the home for shared non-fixture orchestrator test helpers (it holds build_usage_gate).

The new MagicMock factory is named `_make_gate`, the same name as orchestrator/tests/test_usage_gate.py:22's `_make_gate`, which builds a REAL UsageGate; helpers with the same name and opposite meaning coexist in the same test package.

All eight converted call sites (test_invoke.py:489,504,518,532; test_steward.py:1668,1688,1707,1728) pass `before_invoke=AsyncMock(return_value='tok-a')`, identical to the factory default, restating the default at every site and implying the value is site-specific.

The factory builds a bare `MagicMock()` with a `**overrides` setattr passthrough, so it does not enforce its stated invariant: attributes it forgets, attributes renamed or removed on UsageGate, and typo'd override names all silently auto-create truthy mocks (the passthrough of `custom_attr` is even tested as supported). The existing shared.testing.make_gate_mock uses `MagicMock(spec=UsageGate)` for exactly this drift.
The diff deletes an unrelated blank line before `assert captured_kwargs.get('start_new_session') is True` in TestRunSubprocessLocalProcessGroup, outside the refactor's scope.

The TestMakeGateFactory class is duplicated in both test files and mostly tests test scaffolding with assertions that cannot fail meaningfully: `isinstance(gate, MagicMock)` is trivially true, and `test_make_gate_yielding_routes_through_factory` only checks `soonest_resets_at is None`, which the pre-change inline code also satisfied, so it cannot detect whether routing happens. The steward copy's `test_pre_triage_gate_*` tests call `TestPreTriageUsageGateCleanup._gate`, a private static helper of another test class. (The separate gap that these contract tests would not catch a missing default such as detect_cap_hit is frontier_3.)

The steward `_make_gate_yielding` now inherits the factory's `account_count=1` regardless of how many slots it yields, while the test_invoke version passes `account_count=len(slots)`. No current steward test depends on it, but steward's pre-triage path calls invoke_with_cap_retry, which reads `max(usage_gate.account_count, 1)`, so a multi-slot steward gate would model one account.

The new docstrings carry incident history ('122-error cascade (tasks 1313/1339)') in both TestMakeGateFactory classes and make claims the code contradicts: the factory docstring says a new attribute 'only needs to be updated here' though two copies exist, and 'Mirrors the _mock_gate helper' though `_mock_gate` defaults detect_cap_hit and uses different values ('tok'/'acct').

task.title: Extract a shared MagicMock-gate factory for orchestrator tests (mirror shared/tests _mock_gate)
task.description: gate.soonest_resets_at = None was added inline to ~9 separate MagicMock gate construction sites across orchestrator/tests/test_invoke.py and orchestrator/tests/test_steward.py (task 1404). The orchestrator test helpers (_make_gate_yielding and per-test gate setup blocks) repeat the same attribute initialization for on_agent_complete, confirm_account_ok, release_probe_slot, and now soonest_resets_at rather than funneling through one builder, so each new gate attribute requires a shotgun edit touching every site. shared/tests already centralizes this in a _mock_gate helper (test_cap_retry.py:93). Extract an equivalent gate-factory helper for the orchestrator tests so attribute defaults like soonest_resets_at=None are set in one place. Prior bare-MagicMock() gate drift caused a 122-error cascade (tasks 1313/1339), so consolidation has concrete payoff. Scope: refactor only — preserve existing test behavior; route _make_gate_yielding and the standalone gate=MagicMock() builders through the new factory.
